working_title: Breeding-space contraction recurs across spatial scales in Antarctic penguins
central_claim: Declining Antarctic Pygoscelis populations repeatedly show concentration of breeding effort into fewer effective monitored components beyond proportional thinning, and the direction persists from within breeding systems to regional monitored site networks while effect magnitude and component-level routes remain heterogeneous.

evidence_order.scope: species x published APBP region monitored site networks

primary_narrative: abundance decline does not uniquely determine spatial breeding organization
within-system concentration exceeds proportional thinning in five declining trajectories
the same concentration direction appears in all four estimable declining regional networks
direction transfers more consistently than kappa magnitude
Palmer and Signy show different component-level routes to the same endpoint
secondary_descriptive_context: the local abundance-E relationship is stronger over long trajectories than first differences
three increasing regional networks finish with lower E than their first retained complete season
prohibited_claims: formal regional hysteresis or irreversible ratchet
preferential survival of initially largest components as a universal mechanism
closed demographic population interpretation of APBP regions
causal attribution to snow, site fidelity, dispersal, recruitment or predation

supersession.docs/MANUSCRIPT_REPLICATED_CONCENTRATION: retained as provenance; cross-scale v0.1 is the active expanded manuscript
supersession.docs/MANUSCRIPT_INTEGRATED_JBI_V0_4.md: remains superseded; static island-trait null results are not part of the active concentration paper

stop_rule: No further geographic clustering, completeness thresholds, scaling families, lags, trait screens, or same-data mechanism searches are authorized to strengthen the cross-scale claim. New generality requires an independent taxonomic data source.
